title: The Occupation of DC Has Become Ordinary
author: Tanya Golash-Boza
content:
Every day in D.C, caravans of federal agents move through the city. They
accompany local police, surround cars, and participate in arrests. The people
I see detained in these operations are primarily Black men. The agencies and
uniforms vary. The structure remains the same: federal power enters an
ordinary police encounter, and residents have no clear way to know who is in
charge or what rules apply. This is what the past year of federal occupation
has produced in Washington. It is not only soldiers near monuments or
immigration agents carrying out highly visible raids. It is federal power
embedded in everyday policing.
